s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic skin condition with painful nodules and ulceration in the groin area, with a history of intertrigo and recent development of bright red, burning nodules
salient_findings: Bright red, burning and painful nodules around the scrotum
Epidermal ulceration overlying a diffuse dermal proliferation composed of sheets of histiocytes with eosinophilic granular cytoplasm
Intracytoplasmic Michaelis-Gutmann bodies present as basophilic, somewhat laminated intracytoplasmic inclusion bodies
key_facts: 3-month history of intertrigo involving the groin
Treatment with clotrimazole cream, 1%, and hydrocortisone cream, 1% initially improved the condition
Development of bright red, burning and painful nodules around the scrotum after initial improvement
Medical history includes prostate cancer, hypertension, anxiety disorder, hyperlipidemia, gastroesophageal reflux disease, and diverticulosis
Current medications include omeprazole, alprazolam, amlodipine besylate, atenolol, simvastatin, and valsartan
Two symmetrical solitary erythematous nodules present in the right and left inguinal folds adjacent to the scrotum
Histopathological examination showed epidermal ulceration and diffuse dermal proliferation composed of sheets of histiocytes with eosinophilic granular cytoplasm
Intracytoplasmic Michaelis-Gutmann bodies were present and highlighted with iron (Prussian blue) and calcium (Von Kossa) stains
Background population of many plasma cells and few neutrophils noted
Fungus culture was negative
Atypical mycobacteria culture was negative
Bacterial culture was positive for E. coli

shortlist.label: Malakoplakia
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of Michaelis-Gutmann bodies in histopathological examination

shortlist.label: Granuloma inguinale
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic skin condition with painful nodules and ulceration in the groin area

shortlist.label: Hidradenitis suppurativa
shortlist.why_kept: History of intertrigo and development of painful nodules in the groin area

shortlist.label: Erythema nodosum
shortlist.why_kept: Sudden onset of bright red, burning and painful nodules

shortlist.label: Cutaneous tuberculosis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of histiocytes with eosinophilic granular cytoplasm and positive bacterial culture for E. coli

raw.rationale: The presence of Michaelis-Gutmann bodies, which are pathognomonic for Malakoplakia, in the histopathological examination is a strong evidence for this diagnosis. The clinical presentation of erythematous nodules in the inguinal folds and the positive bacterial culture for E. coli also support this diagnosis, as Malakoplakia is often associated with chronic bacterial infections.

rejected.label: Granuloma inguinale
rejected.why: The absence of Donovan bodies in the histopathological examination and the lack of response to typical treatments for Granuloma inguinale make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Hidradenitis suppurativa
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and histopathological findings do not match the typical characteristics of Hidradenitis suppurativa, which usually involves recurrent abscesses and sinus tracts.

rejected.label: Erythema nodosum
rejected.why: The presence of Michaelis-Gutmann bodies and the positive bacterial culture for E. coli are not typical findings in Erythema nodosum, which is usually associated with other underlying conditions such as infections or inflammatory diseases.

rejected.label: Cutaneous tuberculosis
rejected.why: The negative atypical mycobacteria culture and the lack of other typical findings for Cutaneous tuberculosis, such as caseating granulomas, make this diagnosis less likely.
